concepts.def: Vertical (warp) and horizontal (weft) threads interlaced in weaving, the foundation of woven textile structures.
Stencil-based printing technique using mesh screens, used commercially for textiles and by artists from Warhol onwards.
Indonesian wax-resist dyeing technique creating patterns by applying molten wax to areas that resist dye.
Decorative needlework on fabric, ranging from traditional samplers to contemporary art by Tracey Emin.
Unit of design that tiles across a fabric, with options including straight, half-drop and brick repeats.
Process of matting wool fibres together using moisture, heat and pressure, producing dense non-woven fabric.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Textile Design — a core area of GCSE Art & Design.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Textile Design brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Textile Design.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What can line in a composition imply, even without representing an object?
options: Movement, direction, emotion, and visual rhythm.
A composition with no balance.
Only the outline of an object.
Just measurements.
An unbalanced composition.
The space between letters.
A composition with no balance.
Visual equilibrium achieved with different elements of equal visual weight on each side.
